cards.explanation: The answer is that the kingdom might go back to the house of David. Jeroboam says in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.” (1 Kings 12:26) Notice it's a worry he keeps in his heart. Verse 27 shows where it leads, with him picturing the people's hearts returning to Rehoboam king of Judah.

The answer is hearts. Jeroboam says the people's “…hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah…” (1 Kings 12:27) He's not worried about their feet, friends, he's worried about where their hearts end up. I think a man who is scared about that has a lot going on inside.

The answer is True. Jeroboam says, “then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.” (1 Kings 12:27) That is a big thing to be afraid of. Nobody in the passage says it's going to happen, though. It's the picture he paints in his own heart.

The answer is two golden calves, friends. “After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves…” (1 Kings 12:28) The text says he sought advice first, but it doesn't tell us from whom. I'd have wanted a second opinion on that one, and maybe a third.

The answer is that he tells the people the calves are the gods who brought them out of Egypt. He says, “Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.” (1 Kings 12:28) Hold on, friends, because that is a big claim to hang on a calf. The text records what he says, and I'll let that line sit there.

The answer is Dan. “One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.” (1 Kings 12:29) Two calves, two places. Then verse 30 says, “…this thing became a sin…” and that the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.

The answer is people from every class who aren't Levites. Jeroboam “…appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites.” (1 Kings 12:31) The detail to catch is that last part, friends. The text is clear that these priests were not Levites.

The answer is True. Jeroboam “…ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah…” (1 Kings 12:32) So his feast is like the one in Judah. The text also says it was held in “…a month of his own choosing…” (1 Kings 12:33).

The answer is Jeroboam himself. The text says, “…he offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up…” (1 Kings 12:32) The king is up front doing it, friends. He also installs priests in Bethel, but he's the one named at the altar.
The answer is False, friends. The text says it was “…a month of his own choosing…” so Jeroboam picked it himself. (1 Kings 12:33) The date wasn't handed to him. He chose the eighth month on his own.
